data.title: Poiema OBX 2026
data.subtitle: Community, Fellowship, and Truth by the Ocean
data.location: Kill Devil Hills, Outer Banks, NC
data.excerpt: Join young adults and college students for a restorative week on the North Carolina coast with rich fellowship, sound biblical teaching, and ocean hospitality.

children.text: Poiema Retreats gathers young adults from across churches for theological depth, heartfelt worship, and genuine rest. Located right on the shores of Kill Devil Hills, our days feature morning lectures, communal meals, seaside recreation, and evening discussions around Scripture.

data.schedule:
Thursday: Arrival & Welcome Dinner (6:00 PM)
Friday & Saturday: Morning Prayer, Teaching Sessions, Free Ocean Time, Evening Seminar
Sunday: Lord's Day Worship & Feast
Monday: Breakfast & Departure
data.lodging_info: Spacious beachfront houses with shared bedrooms and common spaces for conversation, prayer, and relaxation.

data.schedule:
Friday: Check-in & Campfire Hymn Sing (7:00 PM)
Saturday: Dual Lectures, Hiking / Recreation, Group Discussion
Sunday: Worship & Closing Fellowship

data.title: Created as His Workmanship: The Meaning of Poiema
data.author: Pastor Laurence Windham
data.excerpt: Why Paul chose the word 'poiema' in Ephesians 2:10, and what it means for our redemption and daily callings as God's poetic masterpieces.

children.text: In Ephesians 2:10, the apostle Paul writes: 'For we are His workmanship (ποίημα, poiema), created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them.' We are not haphazard products of fate, nor are we mere cog-like functionaries. The Greek word poiema signifies a crafted work of art, a poem, an intentional masterpiece.

When we gather at Poiema Retreats, our longing is to rediscover what it means to be living expressions of God's grace in our generation. When believers step away from the relentless churn of cultural performance and rest together in Christ, the beauty of that divine workmanship becomes unmistakably clear.

data.title: Living Together in an Age of Loneliness
data.author: Elder David Cooper
data.excerpt: Christian friendship is not an optional hobby. Biblical communion requires intentional time, shared tables, and deep mutual affection.

children.text: Modern life connects us to thousands through glowing screens, yet leaves us uniquely starved for real communion. Dietrich Bonhoeffer reminded us that Christian brotherhood is not an ideal which we must realize, but a reality created by God in Christ in which we may participate.
This is why the retreat format matters so much. A weekend around a common table, breaking bread and singing psalms without urgency, reminds our souls of what we were built for.

children.text: For we are His workmanship (ποίημα), created in Christ Jesus for good works. Poiema Retreats hosts transformative conferences and restful gatherings for college students, singles, and young adults across the East Coast and beyond.

Poiema Retreats was born out of a desire to see young adults rooted deeply in Christian truth, vibrant fellowship, and godly vocation. Operating as a ministry of Saint Peter Presbyterian Church in Bristol, Virginia, we bring together believers from diverse churches to learn, pray, and grow as living works of God's grace.

Poiema Retreats relies on generous gifts to keep retreat ticket prices affordable for college students, provide need-based scholarships, and fund international theological initiatives. Your tax-deductible gift helps build lifelong discipleship.
Have a question about upcoming retreats, registration, speaking, or scholarship assistance? We would love to hear from you.
